title_vi: Vì sao Kafka nhanh: ghi nối tiếp, gom lô, gửi thẳng từ page cache

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Topic, partition và nhật ký của Kafka.
Ghi nối tiếp cũng là ý tưởng của LSM-tree.

claims.evidence: The Persistence and Efficiency sections of the Kafka design page were read from a partial clone of apache/kafka and the producer parameters from librdkafka CONFIGURATION.md; the batching numbers and the sendfile count come from the author's run on Kafka 4.4.0 (three brokers on one machine, confluent-kafka 2.16.0, strace on the leader broker) on 2026-10-18.

Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Kafka relies on the filesystem and the OS pagecache rather than an in-process cache; linear reads and writes are optimised by read-ahead and write-behind; a log of appended files gives O(1) operations instead of B-tree seeks.
claims.section: Persistence: Don't fear the filesystem; Constant Time Suffices
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of apache/kafka at commit 65566690ca1ddb584388c1026e2ff6673e9c6f19.

claims.claim_vi: After disk patterns, the two inefficiencies are too many small I/O operations and excessive byte copying; the protocol groups messages into message sets; a shared binary format lets the broker use sendfile, avoiding the four-copy, two-syscall path so only the final copy to the NIC buffer remains; batches can be compressed end to end and stay compressed on disk and in transit.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of apache/kafka at commit 65566690ca1ddb584388c1026e2ff6673e9c6f19.

claims.claim_vi: TLS/SSL libraries run in user space, so sendfile is not used when SSL is enabled.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of apache/kafka at commit 65566690ca1ddb584388c1026e2ff6673e9c6f19.

claims.claim_vi: librdkafka's linger.ms (alias of queue.buffering.max.ms, default 5) delays sending to build larger batches; batch.num.messages caps messages per MessageSet.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of confluentinc/librdkafka at commit 8c03f75a31ca61d08b2cc2ddc5b233b80d14bdad.

claims.claim_vi: Measured once on Kafka 4.4.0: 50,000 messages of 100 bytes with batch.num.messages=1 took 8.30 s and 50,000 Produce requests; with linger.ms=5 they took 0.07 s and 11 requests; while one consumer read 100,000 messages (a 14.0 MB log segment) strace on the leader broker counted 68 sendfile calls returning 15.6 MB in total.
claims.verified_by: Author's own run on 2026-10-18; request counts from librdkafka statistics; one machine, so network round trips are near zero.

claims.claim_vi: Two design choices make Kafka fast: sequential I/O and zero copy; without zero copy data goes disk, OS cache, application, socket buffer, network card; with zero copy the OS cache sends data to the network card via sendfile().

design_notes_vi: Ba quyết định thiết kế, bốn lần chép của đường thường theo tài liệu Kafka, và số đo thật. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source gives two reasons; the lesson adds batching and batch compression from the Kafka design document and measures batching.
The lesson adds that Kafka does not use sendfile with SSL/TLS, which the source omits.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
